summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish statutory conduct standards and interest registers for parliamentarians, supported by independent advice and a commissioner to examine alleged breaches of conduct codes.
It would create a Parliamentary Integrity Adviser for confidential guidance and a Parliamentary Standards Commissioner to assist with assessing, investigating and resolving alleged code breaches.
The main provisions would depend on funding being appropriated and commencement of the relevant integrity commission provision, while preserving parliamentary powers except where expressly changed.
changes: Conduct duties would extend to staff employed under the parliamentary staffing legislation.
Members and senators would have statutory obligations to register their interests.
People facing critical findings in inquiry reports would receive an opportunity to respond.
Unauthorised recording, use or disclosure of protected integrity information would become an offence, subject to specified exceptions.
summary.affected: Parliamentarians, ministers, their staff, parliamentary committees and the proposed integrity adviser and standards commissioner are affected.
